page: Microsoft Azure E96-48as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration provides 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This server features a substantial memory allocation of 768.0 GB of RAM, translating to 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not include any local storage or GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

In benchmark testing, the E96-48as_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core performance. Its single-core capabilities are highlighted by top-10% placements in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression tests. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, achieving top-10% in Geekbench multi-core and top-25% in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. Memory subsystem performance is strong, with PassMark memory scores in the top 10% and write large block bandwidth in the top 25%, though read-only large block bandwidth falls into the average category.

The combination of high memory density and strong CPU performance makes this server highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, and data analytics. This is supported by its strong performance in Redis SET operations and PassMark database benchmarks. It also handles text processing and software compilation efficiently. However, the lack of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for local-storage-heavy databases or GPU-accelerated deep learning tasks, though it remains capable of moderate CPU-based LLM inference.
